baseline_subtraction_note: This capture is from a current tap dedicated to the HaLow module, not the whole board -- unlike the earlier ESP32-based dataset (see esp-based-code/), there is no board baseline current mixed into these samples, so no baseline estimate/subtraction step is needed before computing energy figures from this CSV.

protocol_pin_encoding.note: (D0, D1) asserted together for the duration of each send call (through the blocking reply wait too, for TCP+reply), (0, 0) between sends -- see adaptive_transport.c's SET_DEBUG_PROTO. Requires ENABLE_PWR_MEAS=1 and D1 (MM_DEBUG_2/PA0) wired to the PPK2's second digital input; a capture from before this pin existed has protocol_pin_encoding absent and a D0-only CSV.

note: Firmware was NOT rebuilt or reflashed for this run -- it is assumed already flashed (e.g. via `make reprogram`) with DEMO_USE_REMOTE_CONFIG=1. L/protocol/atc-*/max-packets above are pushed live to the DUT via server.py's --remote-config on every reset (see remote_config_pushed and the module docstring). remote_config_confirmed is the ground truth for whether that actually took effect this replicate (None means no confirmation was found in the fetched server log; cross-check the captured console log's 'Remote config:' and 'ATC: init' lines, if present). git_commit/git_dirty describe the *source tree*, not necessarily the flashed binary. If remote_config_pushed.MAX_PACKETS > 0, confirm the DUT actually reached it (rather than this capture's --duration/--schedule being too short and silently truncating the run) by checking the captured console log for 'Sent max_packets=' -- its absence means the run was cut off mid-stream, not that MAX_PACKETS failed to apply.
